article.content: Both blocs fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government in initial forecasts as support for Palestinian parties surges Full report: Coalition talks loom as Israel exit polls suggest Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs tied Analysis: Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscape Israel election: what we know so far The lead that exit polls gave to the opposition bloc early in the night has disappeared, with Netanyahu’s grouping now neck and neck with Gadi Eisenkot. Israeli television networks gave the two blocs approximately 51 seats each in the 120 member Knesset – well below the 61 needed to govern. Palestinian parties meanwhile saw a surge in support, with exit polls showing them winning 17 or 18 seats between them. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Vote counting is officially underway across Israel following a general election that early exit polls indicate has resulted in a dead heat between the political bloc led by **Benjamin Netanyahu** and the rival alliance spearheaded by **Gadi Eisenkot**, according to World news | The Guardian. 

Initial television forecasts published late on election night show neither major political grouping securing the **61 seats** required to independently establish a governing majority in the Knesset. As election officials process the ballots, the preliminary figures point toward protracted coalition negotiations to break the legislative deadlock, reflecting a deeply divided electorate as tracked in our ongoing coverage of how [Israel's election has a high turnout, lifting opposition hopes of beating Netanyahu](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/israel-s-election-has-a-high-turnout-lifting-opposition-hopes-of-beating). 

## Rising Turnout and Surging Palestinian Support

A notable driver of the tight race was a significant surge in voter backing for Palestinian parties, which dramatically altered the parliamentary arithmetic projected by initial exit polls, the report states. Analysts tracking the vote noted that high civic participation overall gave opposition figures renewed momentum throughout polling day, mirroring trends observed as [Israel goes to the polls in most consequential election in its history – live updates](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/israel-goes-to-the-polls-in-most-consequential-election-in-its-history). 

While early broadcasts offered a glimpse into the national mood, official tallying bodies caution that final results could shift as remote and specialized polling stations report their numbers. The razor-thin margins have left political analysts emphasizing that [Israel election too close to call as exit polls give Netanyahu bloc slightly fewer seats](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/israel-election-too-close-to-call-as-exit-polls-give-netanyahu-bloc), setting the stage for tense days ahead.

## Political Stakes and Potential Coalitions

*Context: Parliamentary systems rely on stable coalitions to govern, meaning that even a tie in overall seat distribution forces major parties to court smaller factions, religious groups, or minority representatives. For international observers and domestic citizens alike, the stakes of this electoral stalemate center on governance continuity, economic policy, and regional security approaches.*

*What to watch: Observers will be monitoring the formal certification of vote counts by the central election committee, as well as any early signals from smaller parties regarding potential alliance-building.*

Sources: [World news | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/oct/28/israel-election-results-live-updates-exit-polls-netanyahu-likud-eisenkot-latest-news)
